title: Diagnostic Concierge: Guided Failure Triage Card & Payload Lens
creator: Aisha Marquez
description:
Problem: Customers and internal SREs repeatedly ask for a faster path from an alert or failed API request to a focused troubleshooting surface. Current consoles show lists of failed requests, but engineers spend too much time context-switching between request rows, raw payload blobs, and separate trace dashboards.

Opportunity: Introduce a compact, persistent 'Diagnostic Concierge' card in the Console list and rollout detail pages that surfaces an actionable triage workflow for a selected failed request: curated failure summary, likely error taxonomy, quick retry controls, side-by-side payload diff, KV cache snapshot links, and a lightweight local replay button. The card should be usable in small screens and support keyboard navigation.

Goals:
- Reduce mean time to triage (MTTT) for failed inference calls by 30% for common classes (model runtime error, OOM, network timeout, malformed request).
- Provide designers and engineers a single entrypoint for the most common triage actions (inspect payload, compare retries, re-run with safe sandbox inputs).
- Be composable into existing Console list rows and rollout canary panels without increasing visual noise.

Non-goals: Full incident playbook automation, replacing deep trace analysis pages, or implementing automated root-cause detection in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostic Concierge card appears as a collapsible right rail on Request list and rollout canary pages and opens via keyboard shortcut 'd' when a row is focused.
Card shows a one-line failure taxonomy tag (e.g., runtime-error, kv-miss, rate-limit) derived from the tracing metadata and provides links to full trace where available.
Payload Lens supports toggleable views: Raw JSON, Pretty/Schema-validated view, and Retry Comparison diff between last two attempts.
Replay button launches a sandboxed dry-run request and surfaces result logs without sending tokens to production model backends (uses stubbed backend in dev mode).
Design handoff includes Figma frames, interaction notes, and an annotated accessibility checklist (keyboard, screen reader labels, contrast ratios).
design_rationale: Users are interrupted by too many discrete surfaces when debugging. A focused, collapsible rail that accumulates context (request history, retry chain, error taxonomy) reduces navigation. We prefer progressive disclosure — show high-value signals first (taxonomy, top 3 headers, short payload preview) and allow dives for full payload and diffs. The design emphasizes low visual weight to avoid competing with primary metrics in rollout pages.
ux_research_findings: Interviewed 6 platform engineers: 5 reported needing payload diffs as the most time-consuming step.
Average time to find the failing field in payloads > 7 minutes without a diff tool.
Engineers prefer a single keyboard-first flow over clicking multiple links into separate pages.
